- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.28) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast by 1–2% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows repeated negative spikes (e.g., -0.28, -0.28), model tends to lag — delay correction by 1–2 days and adjust downward gradually.
- If model forecast is >+2% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly positive.
- Model often overestimates volatility in early horizon — reduce forecast variance by 10–20% for first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- When sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days.
